analysis: The PR modifies only docs/developer/test.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date (head line 3), adds a test command `python3 scripts/test-provider-cluster-runtime-models.py` (head ~1289), and extends the release-test prose (head ~1325-1340, 1353-1356) to describe cluster_runtime block checks. These checks cover malformed-block refusal, 128-byte derived-ID limits, the 64 KiB registration body limit enforced before staging, and a local-HTTP-registry model-metadata fetch that reads no weights and uses no network. The base/head text units supplied (base lines 2309-2510, head lines 1-463) are mostly unchanged surrounding content. The changed ranges themselves fall outside the visible head excerpt, so I could not verify the changed lines directly. They are visible only via the truncated patch excerpt. No code, configuration, endpoint, key handling, attestation, cache, or authorization behavior changes. The documentation describes tests that tighten validation (registration size and field bounds) and imposes no new attack surface. There is no change to threat-model assets, boundaries or mitigations (T-041 SSD cache unchanged; the SSD test working volume text is existing context). Remaining unverified items: the truncated patch excerpt (cuts off at `scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh`), and the scripts and tests it references, which are outside the supplied evidence. Nothing here is evidence of a regression. A deeper review of the actual cluster_runtime validation code and tests would be needed in any other batch.
